# Variants

## extends

Keywords: `extends`.

First line of a variant: the id of the screen it changes.

Content: yes. Container: yes.
Options: none. No common flags or id.

```text
extends: base
```

## replace

Keywords: `replace`.

In a variant: replace the component with this id by the one under it.

Content: yes. Container: yes.
Options: none. No common flags or id.

```text
extends: base
replace: target
  text: Updated
```

## remove

Keywords: `remove`.

In a variant: remove the components with these ids.

Content: yes. Container: no.
Options: none. No common flags or id.

```text
extends: base
remove: target
```

## after

Keywords: `after`.

In a variant: add the components under it after the one with this id.

Content: yes. Container: yes.
Options: none. No common flags or id.

```text
extends: base
after: target
  text: Updated
```

## before

## rows

Keywords: `rows`.

In a variant: change, add or remove rows of the grid with this id.

Content: yes. Container: no.
Options: none. No common flags or id.

```text

```

## Variants

Start with extends: screen-id. Use replace: id with exactly one indented
component (it inherits the id; with no children of its own and the
target's type, it keeps the target's children), remove: id (comma-separated ids allowed),
after: id or before: id with indented additions, and rows: grid-id with
indented rows. In rows, = keeps a cell and remove <row-key> removes a row.
Here is a base screen and a variant using every verb:

```wiredown
window: Members
  text: Original #title
  text: Temporary #temporary
  grid #target
  Name | Status
  Anna | Invited
  Erik | Active
```

^base

```wiredown
extends: base
replace: title
  text: Updated
remove: temporary
before: target
  text: Before table
after: target
  text: After table
rows: target
  Anna | Active
  remove Erik
```

^updated
